## Summary

This report replaces the earlier 12-case smoke test as the headline benchmark. The new corpus has **240 deterministic synthetic cases** (120 memories, 192 train / 48 holdout). The holdout is fixed by the generator and was not used to choose retrieval weights.

The README table and the table below are generated from the current post-fix run at `562f461`. The earlier v0.2.0 snapshot at `1495622` is preserved as [`bench/results/minilm-1495622.json`](../bench/results/minilm-1495622.json) for comparison.

| Configuration | Split | Hit@1 | Hit@3 | Hit@5 | MRR | nDCG@10 | Context tokens | p50 |
| :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| FastrMemory + MiniLM | Train | 96.4% | 99.0% | 100% | 0.976 | 0.982 | 208 | 3.30 ms |
| FastrMemory + MiniLM | **Holdout** | **95.8%** | **97.9%** | **100%** | **0.969** | **0.977** | 209 | 3.41 ms |
| BM25-only | Train | 79.7% | 90.6% | 100% | 0.868 | 0.900 | 203 | 0.48 ms |
| BM25-only | **Holdout** | 77.1% | 77.1% | 93.8% | 0.804 | 0.835 | 204 | 0.60 ms |
| Static dump - simulated | Train | 2.1% | 6.3% | 8.3% | 0.055 | 0.081 | 3652 | 0.00 ms |

The raw JSON stores bootstrap 95% CIs for triple-stream Hit@1: train **93.8-98.4%**, holdout **89.6-100%**. The Wilson 95% CI for the 46/48 holdout result is **86.0-98.9%**; with 48 cases the interval is wide. Hit@5 is 100% on both splits.

## What changed from the 12-case suite

- The old suite had 12 hand-written cases and simulated rows that were easy to over-read. It remains available as a smoke test but is not the headline.
- The new suite has six categories, a fixed 80/20 split, and bootstrap confidence intervals.
- Retrieval defaults were tuned only on train: RRF `k = 20`, MiniLM vector weight `3.0`, title + module semantic vectors, and conditional trap boosting.
- The Phase 2 fix includes `module` in the embedding document during backfill; the earlier run embedded `module: undefined` because the backfill query did not select that column.
- Context measurement now separates the **ranked result set** from the **compact prompt text**. The prompt text is capped at 250 tokens; the full ranked memories remain available to the caller.

## Per-category results (triple-stream, MiniLM)

| Category | Train cases | Train Hit@1 | Train Hit@5 | Holdout cases | Holdout Hit@1 | Holdout Hit@5 |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Exact keyword | 48 | 100% | 100% | 12 | 100% | 100% |
| Semantic paraphrase | 48 | 85.4% | 100% | 12 | 83.3% | 100% |
| File-scoped trap | 32 | 100% | 100% | 8 | 100% | 100% |
| Bi-temporal superseded | 32 | 100% | 100% | 8 | 100% | 100% |
| Multi-hop | 16 | 100% | 100% | 4 | 100% | 100% |
| Long-horizon | 16 | 100% | 100% | 4 | 100% | 100% |

All categories except semantic paraphrase are saturated at Hit@1. Paraphrase remains the retrieval gap: the holdout is 83.3% Hit@1, although every paraphrase target is still in the top 5. The failures are title-concept collisions where several memories share a broad term and the query describes a narrower behavior.

## Ablations

| Configuration | Train Hit@1 | Holdout Hit@1 | Interpretation |
| :--- | ---: | ---: | :--- |
| BM25-only | 79.7% | 77.1% | Lexical baseline inside FastrMemory |
| BM25 + MiniLM | 96.4% | 95.8% | Title + module semantic vectors add the largest gain |
| BM25 + file graph | 79.7% | 77.1% | Graph alone does not add Hit@1 on this corpus |
| Triple-stream, production defaults | 96.4% | 95.8% | Graph and conditional trap boost are neutral here |
| Hash embeddings | 81.8% | 77.1% | Offline fallback; lexical duplicate of BM25 |

The graph stream is retained because real repositories contain file-linked memories that share no query terms; this synthetic corpus does not exercise that case beyond memories that are already rank 1. The conditional trap boost is retained so the 2.0x multiplier applies only to trap-intent queries or queries scoped to a linked file, instead of boosting every trap regardless of context.

## Why the holdout is lower

The holdout contains 12 paraphrase cases, so one miss costs 8.3 points. The holdout point estimate is noisy: the raw JSON bootstrap 95% CI is 89.6-100%, and the Wilson 95% CI is 86.0-98.9%. The correct reading is:

- Exact, file, temporal, multi-hop, and long-horizon behavior is solved on this corpus.
- Semantic paraphrase is the remaining gap: 83.3% holdout Hit@1, but every target is recovered in the top 5.
- More paraphrase data and a reranker are the next retrieval work, not a claim that the current system is at 95.8% on real codebases.

## Limitations

1. **Synthetic, generated cases.** Not SWE-bench, LongMemEval, or LoCoMo. The corpus tests defined retrieval behaviors, not general coding-agent competence.
2. **No external engine measured.** The static-dump row is a local simulation, not another project.
3. **Small holdout.** Forty-eight cases; bootstrap Hit@1 interval is 89.6-100%, Wilson interval is 86.0-98.9%.
4. **Token counts are estimates**, not tokenizer-exact.
5. **Latency is in-process** and excludes Node startup and model load.
6. **MiniLM is optional.** The offline hash path is much weaker on paraphrase.

## Reproduce

```bash
npm ci
npx tsx scripts/eval-bench.ts --split all --embeddings minilm --out bench/results/minilm.json
npx tsx scripts/eval-bench.ts --split all --embeddings hash --out bench/results/hash.json
```

The JSON includes every case result, per-category metrics, bootstrap CIs, and the exact commit. Accuracy should reproduce; latency will vary by machine.
